reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) directly supports Zr diffusion into Hf to form a HfZr transition layer and reduced weight gain, but only on a VZrHfNbTa HEA substrate, not on Zr-alloy cladding. The hypothesis extrapolates this mechanism to a different substrate and a thinner coating without direct evidence, leaving key premises about transferability and the oxygen barrier role unsupported.
premises: Zirconium diffuses into hafnium coating to form a HfZr alloy transition layer
The HfZr transition layer acts as an effective oxygen diffusion barrier
Hafnium coating significantly reduces oxide weight gain vs. uncoated substrate
The protective mechanism is demonstrated on a VZrHfNbTa HEA substrate
The coating process and thickness (sub-micron to micron) are transferable to Zr-alloy cladding
